notes.1: Most candidates answered this question correctly. However, some selected photosynthesis as the answer showing a misunderstanding of the process involved.
notes.6: Plant cell structure posed few problems for candidates. The presence of a cell wall in both diagrams was recognised by all candidates and with nearly all recognising chloroplasts in one cell and not in the other.
notes.9: The reference to transport as a function of xylem, appears to have been a distraction from the fact that the xylem is a tissue and not an organ. Some candidates therefore missed the fact that the xylem is a tissue used for support.
notes.11: This question proved challenging as many overlooked the fact that absorption in the ileum will occur by diffusion and that there is no form of gas exchange occurring in the bronchioles.
notes.12: Candidates should remember that digestion occurring in the stomach does so in strongly acidic conditions. Clearly they knew that enzymes are not sugars, but some also believed that all of them are most effective at pH7.
notes.15: This proved to be a challenging question as some candidates erroneously believed that the liver produces digestive enzymes.
notes.18: Some candidates showed a good understanding of the function of the phloem.
notes.22: Accommodation proved to be a particularly challenging concept for many candidates.
notes.24: Some candidates were thought that diffusion occurs in the umbilical cord rather than the placenta. Questions 28 and 37 Were questions that demanded the ability to read information from a graph and candidates showed that this is a skill they have mastered, with a very high percentage of correct answers seen in both questions.
notes.30: The traditional confusion between meiosis and mitosis was seen, as was an uncertainty over the function of meiosis.
notes.general_comments:
The paper worked well to provide a meaningful challenge to candidates at this level. The most challenging
questions served to expose some underlying uncertainties in candidates’ minds, and, otherwise, all
questions made a significant contribution to discriminating between candidates of differing abilities.
